stories.title: Jio Platforms announces Rs 30,213 crore IPO with valuation above Rs 10 lakh crore
stories.summary: Jio Platforms disclosed a mega initial public offering with an issue size of Rs 30,213 crore and a valuation exceeding Rs 10 lakh crore, making it the largest public issue in India to date. The announcement highlighted that the prospectus provides information on the IPO dates, price band and guaranteed minimum price (GMP) for investors.
stories.why: The scale of the offering establishes a new benchmark for Indian capital markets and signals strong investor interest in the telecom sector.

stories.title: India’s unemployment rate steady at 5% in September 2026
stories.summary: India’s overall unemployment rate held steady at 5.0% in September 2026, unchanged from the previous month. Rural unemployment fell to 4.2%, while urban unemployment rose slightly to 6.9% and urban female unemployment increased to 9.2%; the Labour Force Participation Rate rose to 55.5% year‑on‑year and the Worker Population Ratio climbed to 52.7%.
stories.why: The data show a stable overall job market but divergent rural‑urban trends, informing policymakers and investors.

stories.title: RBI clarifies FERR does not apply to market‑making, proprietary trading, ECB interest or NR dividends
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India said the foreign exchange risk reserve (FERR) requirement is not applicable to banks that conduct market‑making or proprietary trading. It also clarified that the rule does not affect interest payments on external commercial borrowings (ECBs) or dividends payable to non‑resident investors. Banks must retain the FERR until one day after the related derivative contract ends.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: IMF applauds India’s GDP data revamp, cites strong fundamentals amid energy shock
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund praised India’s recent overhaul of its gross domestic product data and said the country entered an energy shock while maintaining strong economic fundamentals. The IMF’s comment reflects a positive assessment of the data revision and the underlying economy.
stories.why: The IMF’s assessment can influence confidence in India’s economic data, policy credibility and macroeconomic outlook.

stories.title: School headscarf ban sparks rare protests in Azerbaijan and row with Turkey
stories.summary: "You are telling me, I can't come to school?" says a teenage girl in a navy blue Islamic headscarf, captured on video challenging a staff member at the entrance to her school. The footage has been shared widely on social media, and shows a group of girls in hijabs standing behind her applauding as she continues: "Why should I have to give up my religion?" Last Monday the education ministry in Azerbaijan began enforcing new uniform rules, turning away female pupils wearing hijabs.

stories.title: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills two, minister says
stories.summary: Two security personnel have been killed in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally-recognised government, officials say. Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya Zindani condemned the Houthis' attack on Aden, calling it "cowardly" and a "continuation of their criminal behaviour".

stories.title: Student protests in Tirana turn violent, targeting ministries
stories.summary: Thousands of students marched in Tirana on the second day of anti‑government protests that began outside the Ministry of Education on Tuesday. On Wednesday, part of the education ministry building was set on fire and the prime minister’s office, finance and interior ministries, as well as nearby businesses, were attacked. Dozens of protesters wearing gas masks and balaclavas threw rocks and firecrackers at the education ministry’s gates.
stories.why: The unrest highlights student dissatisfaction with university conditions and job prospects, which could affect Albania’s social stability.

stories.previousSummary: Thousands of students have taken to the streets in the Albanian capital of Tirana, attacking several government buildings on the second day of violent anti-government protests.
